Imbolc Awakening Herbal Tea

Served at: Imbolc Day Celebration

Serves 4Prep 5 minCook 10 min (steeping)

This invigorating herbal tea is a perfect way to celebrate Imbolc, a festival of purification, new beginnings, and the first stirrings of spring. Featuring cleansing nettle, refreshing peppermint, and aromatic rosemary, it's a warming brew to honor the returning light and prepare for the growing season ahead.

Ingredients

  • 1 tablespoon (15 mL) dried nettle leaf
  • 1 tablespoon (15 mL) dried peppermint leaf
  • 1 teaspoon (5 mL) dried rosemary
  • 1 strip fresh lemon peel (about 1 inch / 2.5 cm long)
  • 4 cups (950 mL) boiling water
  • Honey or maple syrup, to taste (optional)

Method

  1. Gather your dried herbs and fresh lemon peel.
  2. Place the dried nettle, peppermint, rosemary, and fresh lemon peel into a heatproof teapot or French press.
  3. Bring 4 cups (950 mL) of fresh water to a rolling boil.
  4. Carefully pour the boiling water over the herbs and lemon peel in the teapot.
  5. Cover the teapot with a lid to keep the heat and aromatic oils contained.
  6. Allow the tea to steep for 7-10 minutes, or longer for a stronger brew.
  7. Strain the tea into individual mugs, discarding the spent herbs and lemon peel.
  8. Sweeten with honey or maple syrup to taste, if desired.
  9. Serve warm and mindfully enjoy the invigorating essence of Imbolc.

Tips

  • Vary the herbs: Experiment with other Imbolc-appropriate herbs like dried elderflower, dandelion root, or a slice of fresh ginger for different flavors and properties.
  • Fresh herbs: If using fresh herbs, use 2-3 times the amount of dried herbs for a more vibrant flavor.
  • Mindful moment: Take a quiet moment while sipping your tea to reflect on new beginnings and the returning light of spring, setting intentions for the season ahead.
